scope: Company-local internal timesheet projects, separate from app/projects.py and local database catalogs.

response.approver_candidates: Only administrators: list of active approved accounts with hr.view_own, each {user_id,name}. Others receive [].

projects.visibility: Non-administrators receive active projects; administrators receive all. Existing weekly records include their current project metadata even when inactive. can_submit means project active and at least one active designated approver other than the current user, not a grant of hr.timesheets_submit.

save_payload.id: Existing UUID; omitted or empty string only for new project
save_payload.version: 0 new; exact current version for existing
save_payload.name: Required, maximum 160 chars, casefold-unique including inactive names
approver_ids: Current active approved hr.view_own account UUIDs

projects.authorization: Named current administrator only. Audited and idempotent; no implicit account grants or production assignments. Removing/disabling a project or approver revokes project review immediately. Replay rechecks current authorization.

week.period: week_start must be Monday; week_end is Sunday. ISO dates are local work dates, not UTC instants.

records: Presented project-linked timesheet records in this exact week, including submitted, approved and rejected locked records
projects: Current project metadata for active choices and all existing records
legacy_records: Existing projectless records overlapping this week; read-only here and edited with existing legacy editor

week.visibility: Own week is allowed with hr.view_own. Other users only under existing global timesheet-review scope; designated project reviewers use scoped records/review queue, never another person's complete week.

record_additions.project: Presented current project or inactive metadata
record_additions.can_edit: Owner, submit capability and draft/returned; inactive project is not editable
record_additions.can_submit: Editable, nonempty and independent active designated approver
record_additions.can_review: Currently submitted, designated active approver, not author

save_payload.user_id: Own UUID; optional defaults to current user

records.id: Existing timesheet UUID; omit for new
records.version: Exact current record version; 0 for new

entries.hours: Decimal string from 0 through 24, at most 2 decimal places; zero must be explicit, never inferred
entries.location: Optional work location, maximum 240 chars; preserves legacy optionality

records.notes: Optional record notes, max4000 chars; omission preserves existing record notes, explicit empty string clears current value with history retained.

save_semantics: records contains only changed projects; each entry replaces that project's week completely, not a per-day patch.
At most one record per user+week+project; duplicate dates within a project rejected. Same date across different projects allowed.
Existing IDs and exact versions required; only draft/returned records editable. Never alter another user's record.
Daily sum across all persisted timesheets for this user, including untouched projects and legacy records, must remain <=24. All changes validate and commit together or none do.
Removing every line of an existing project keeps the same record as an empty draft with history. A new project requires at least one entry. No deletions.
All edits share one operation receipt. Exact replay returns current authorized week without duplicating writes; changed payload under same op_id rejected.
No inferred 8-hour days, work schedules, wages, payroll or expenses. No timesheet attachments.
week.save_response: Same structure as GET timesheet-week after the whole transaction commits.

workflow.submit_action: submit_timesheet with existing {id,version} payload, individually per project
workflow.review_action: review_timesheet with existing {id,version,decision:approve|return|reject,comment} payload, individually per project
workflow.review_rules: Project-linked records require current project designation for every reviewer, including admin/global HR reviewer, and prohibit own approval/return/rejection. Project must be active; reviewer must remain enabled/approved with hr.view_own. Global HR rights permit reading as before, but cannot approve without designation. Records without project retain legacy rules.
workflow.reviewer_visibility: Designation plus hr.view_own grants only submitted, approved or rejected timesheets for assigned projects, never drafts or returned records (which the author may edit), documents, expenses, full people records or other projects. Queue/pending actions show only currently actionable submitted records; history rechecks current project access. Revocation takes effect on reads, writes and retries.
workflow.returned_record_visibility: Returned records are private to owner and pre-existing global HR reader scope until resubmitted. Restricted project reviewers cannot read returned current data or history. Project linkage is immutable on each record, including all historical snapshots.
workflow.approval_count: Any one currently designated independent approver. No all-approvers consensus or partial approvals.

errors: Use existing HTTP Problem {detail,...} conventions; 401 account changed, 403 unauthorized own/action, 404 hidden record, 409 stale version/receipt or locked state, 422 invalid inputs/daily total/approver availability. New authored text supports pt-BR via hr_text context and defaults to English.

directory_flags.timesheet_project_review: Top-level boolean: active project currently designates current user
directory_flags.timesheet_projects_manage: Top-level boolean: current named administrator; does not mutate account permission capabilities

storage_compatibility: First project configuration atomically promotes hr_meta.format to wavelink-hr-2. UI129 accepts formats1/2; format2 requires hr_timesheet_projects already present. UI128 fails closed on format2, so code-only downgrade after use is unsupported; restore a compatible verified backup instead.
